subject: math.SG
name: Weinstein conjecture in higher dimensions
statement: Does every Reeb vector field on every closed cooriented contact manifold of dimension at least five have a periodic orbit?
importance: It predicts the existence of closed trajectories for a broad class of constrained Hamiltonian systems.
status_note: The three-dimensional case is proved, as are many higher-dimensional cases with extra hypotheses; the general higher-dimensional statement remains open.

subject: math.SG
name: Nearby Lagrangian conjecture
statement: For every closed connected smooth manifold Q, is every closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of T*Q Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section?
importance: It asks whether cotangent bundles contain any genuinely different closed exact Lagrangian geometry.
status_note: Exactness refers to the restriction of the canonical Liouville form. Strong homotopy-equivalence results are known but do not establish Hamiltonian isotopy in general.

references.title: Simple Homotopy Equivalence of Nearby Lagrangians

subject: math.SG
name: Arnold chord conjecture in higher dimensions
statement: For every contact form on a closed contact manifold of dimension at least five and every closed Legendrian submanifold L, does the Reeb flow have a nonconstant finite-time trajectory with both endpoints on L?
importance: It is a fundamental intersection and recurrence question for Legendrian submanifolds.
status_note: The three-dimensional case is proved. Endpoints are allowed to coincide: demanding distinct endpoints is a stronger assertion with counterexamples.

references.title: Proof of the Arnold chord conjecture in three dimensions II

subject: math.SG
name: Symplectic isotopy conjecture for plane curves
statement: Is every smooth connected embedded symplectic surface in (CP^2, ω_FS) symplectically isotopic to a smooth complex algebraic curve?
importance: It asks whether symplectic geometry allows new smooth plane-curve types beyond algebraic geometry.
status_note: The assertion is proved through degree 17; unrestricted higher-degree smooth curves remain open. Singular-curve variants have different answers.

references.title: A new approach to the symplectic isotopy problem

subject: math.SG
name: Uniqueness of symplectic forms on higher projective spaces
statement: For n at least three, is every symplectic form on CP^n cohomologous to the Fubini–Study form carried to that form by a diffeomorphism?
importance: It tests whether a basic algebraic manifold admits any exotic symplectic geometry.
status_note: Uniqueness is known for CP^2 after normalization; the corresponding higher-dimensional classification is unresolved.

subject: math.SG
name: Homotopy type of higher projective-space symplectomorphism groups
statement: Determine the homotopy type of Symp(CP^n, ω_FS) for n at least three; in particular, is the inclusion PU(n+1) into this group a homotopy equivalence?
importance: It seeks to compare the full nonlinear symmetry group with the classical projective unitary symmetries.
status_note: The analogous statement for CP^2 follows from Gromov’s work; the higher-dimensional problem remains open.

subject: math.SG
name: Unboundedness of Hofer’s metric
statement: Does the group Ham(M, ω) have infinite diameter in Hofer’s metric for every closed connected positive-dimensional symplectic manifold (M, ω)?
importance: It asks whether Hamiltonian transformations always exhibit arbitrarily large symplectic energy cost.
status_note: Unboundedness is known for many manifolds; the unrestricted assertion for all closed symplectic manifolds remains open.

references.title: The Geometry of the Group of Symplectic Diffeomorphism

subject: math.SG
name: C^0 flux conjecture
statement: Is Ham(M, ω) closed inside the identity component Symp_0(M, ω) in the C^0 topology for every closed symplectic manifold?
importance: It asks whether the Hamiltonian condition survives uniform limits that remain smooth symplectomorphisms.
status_note: C^1 closedness follows from the proved flux conjecture; C^0 closedness is known in various cases but remains open in general.

subject: math.SG
name: Closed-characteristic multiplicity conjecture
statement: Does every smooth compact hypersurface in R^(2n) that is strictly star-shaped with respect to the origin carry at least n geometrically distinct simple closed characteristics, for every n at least three?
importance: It predicts the minimum number of periodic trajectories forced by the geometry of a Hamiltonian energy surface.
status_note: Recent results establish this bound for dynamically convex Reeb flows. The unrestricted star-shaped case, without convexity or nondegeneracy assumptions, remains open.

references.title: Closed Orbits of Dynamically Convex Reeb Flows: Towards the HZ- and Multiplicity Conjectures

subject: math.SG
name: Smooth local middle-dimensional non-squeezing
statement: For a smooth symplectic embedding φ defined near a point x in R^(2n) and orthogonal projection P onto a complex linear subspace of real dimension 2k, with 1 less than k less than n, must vol_(2k)(Pφ(B(x,r))) be at least the volume of B^(2k)(r) for all sufficiently small positive r?
importance: It asks whether local symplectic rigidity controls projections in dimensions between two and the full ambient dimension.
status_note: The local assertion is proved for real-analytic embeddings; unrestricted global middle-dimensional non-squeezing is false. The smooth local version remains open.

references.title: Local middle dimensional symplectic non-squeezing in the analytic setting
